findings.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P2/100] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" Adding the same hostname with two different categories succeeds because neither the model nor schema enforces hostname uniqueness, after which imports always select the first matching row and ignore category edits to the other row.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P2/100] "host = uri.host" Saving the accepted hostname example.com:8443 creates an unusable mapping because lookup strips the request port and compares example.com against the stored example.com:8443, preventing that host from embedding and its articles from resolving their configured category.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — [P2/100] "validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i" The new five-character top-level-domain limit rejects valid hosts such as example.technology, so administrators cannot create or edit embedding mappings for those domains.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2/100] "host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));" Saving a host with the category chooser cleared persists the server's uncategorized default but then overwrites the client category with the unresolved null selection, leaving the displayed relationship inconsistent with the saved relationship until reload.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — [P3/100] "render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, root: 'embedding', rest_serializer: true)" The aggregate PUT endpoint returns success while discarding every submitted change, so delete the unused update action, its PUT route, and the unreachable saveChanges client action to keep category/host mutations owned by EmbeddableHostsController; rebuttal: the endpoint scaffolds future aggregate settings; survives because: no aggregate setting is writable today and the exposed success response falsely promises persistence to callers.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1/100] "execute \"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\"" Migrating an existing allowed host such as `https://example.com/articles` stores the unnormalized URL directly, bypassing the model callback, so the new hostname-only lookup rejects previously functioning embeds after upgrade.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — [P2/100] "validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i" The five-letter TLD limit prevents administrators from adding valid hosts such as `example.museum` or saving category edits for those hosts after migration, although the previous host lookup accepted them.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P2/100] "host = uri.host" Saving the explicitly permitted host `example.com:8080` retains the port in the database while lookup strips it from `http://example.com:8080/article`, so that successfully saved host never authorizes embedding or supplies its configured category.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P2/100] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" Creating two allowed-host rows for the same hostname with different categories succeeds because there is no uniqueness constraint, but lookup uses only one row, so category edits to the other row have no effect on imported topics.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — [P1/100] "[0]['id'].to_i" An installation with the default empty embed_category, no persisted embed_category setting, or a deleted/renamed configured category returns zero joined rows and raises at [0] before the fallback runs, aborting the database upgrade even when embedding is unused.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1/100] "VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)" Migrating a previously supported entry such as https://example.com/1234 stores the full URL without the new model's normalization callback, so record_for_host's comparison against example.com never matches and existing embedded comments stop working after upgrade.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1/75] "VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)" A legacy URL entry containing an apostrophe in its path, such as https://example.com/it's, breaks the unescaped SQL string literal and aborts the entire migration; rebuttal: the old setting description requested hostname-only values; survives because: the old lookup explicitly parsed URL entries and its existing controller specifications exercised hosts with schemes and paths, so normalization and SQL quoting remain necessary for supported stored data.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [P2/100] "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')" A rollback to the previous application version loses its embedding configuration because the migration deletes both source settings without any reverse data transformation; rebuttal: a one-way migration can intentionally retire obsolete settings; survives because: the previous version reads only those settings, and retaining the new table supplies no usable configuration to that version.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — [P1/100] "[0]['id'].to_i" Running the migration on a database without an embed_category setting matching an existing category returns zero rows and raises when indexing row zero, aborting the upgrade before the uncategorized fallback or host migration executes.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2/100] "host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));" Changing the still-enabled category chooser from A to B while a save of A is in flight makes the success callback display B as saved even though the server persisted A; rebuttal: the save and cancel buttons are disabled during the request; survives because: the category chooser remains enabled and the callback reads its current value instead of the saved request or response.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — [P2/100] "this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => {" A rejected DELETE request leaves an unhandled promise rejection with no deletion error rendered by this component, so the administrator receives no actionable explanation for the host remaining in the table; rebuttal: removal occurs only after success and a global rejection hook can log the error; survives because: neither logging nor retaining the row tells the administrator that deletion failed, and this action omits the popupAjaxError handler already used by save.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15 — [P2/100] "host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first" Updating or deleting a host removed by another administrator dereferences nil in save_host or host.destroy and returns an unhandled server error instead of a missing-record response; rebuttal: the UI normally submits IDs from its loaded host list; survives because: that list remains stale after another session deletes a host and neither mutation action checks the lookup result.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — [P2/100] "self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')" Creating or updating with an embeddable_host payload whose host is null or omitted raises NoMethodError before format validation and bypasses the controller's validation-error response; rebuttal: the current form disables saving an empty host; survives because: the server accepts direct API requests and assigns the missing or null value before invoking this callback.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P2/100] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" Adding the same hostname with two different categories succeeds because neither the model nor schema enforces hostname uniqueness, after which imports always select the first matching row and ignore category edits to the other row.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff: 1) The EmbeddableHost model in app/models/embeddable_host.rb has no uniqueness validation on the 'host' field - only a format validation. 2) The migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table without a unique index on 'host'. 3) The record_for_host method uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which will return only the first matching record if duplicates exist. 4) In topic_embed.rb, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` is used to determine the category for embedded topics, meaning if duplicate hosts exist with different categories, only the first one's category will ever be used. This is a legitimate data integrity bug where duplicate hostnames can be created, leading to confusing behavior where category changes on duplicate entries are silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P2/100] "host = uri.host" Saving the accepted hostname example.com:8443 creates an unusable mapping because lookup strips the request port and compares example.com against the stored example.com:8443, preventing that host from embedding and its articles from resolving their configured category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the code. Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `record_for_host` method extracts only `uri.host` (line 14: `host = uri.host`) which strips the port. However, the `before_validation` callback (lines 5-7) only strips the protocol and path from the stored host value, preserving any port number. The validation regex on line 2 explicitly allows ports: `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. So if a user saves 'example.com:8443', it's stored with the port, but lookups compare against just 'example.com' (without port), causing a mismatch. This is a legitimate correctness bug where hosts with ports won't match.

Looking at lines 32-38 of embeddable-host.js.es6: when categoryId is null/empty (user cleared the category chooser), the server-side code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 24 sets it to uncategorized_category_id as a default. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P2/100] "host = uri.host" Saving the explicitly permitted host `example.com:8080` retains the port in the database while lookup strips it from `http://example.com:8080/article`, so that successfully saved host never authorizes embedding or supplies its configured category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the code. Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback strips the protocol and path from the host (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), but it does NOT strip the port. This is a legitimate correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [P2/100] "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')" A rollback to the previous application version loses its embedding configuration because the migration deletes both source settings without any reverse data transformation; rebuttal: a one-way migration can intentionally retire obsolete settings; survives because: the previous version reads only those settings, and retaining the new table supplies no usable configuration to that version.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration deletes the old site_settings ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') after migrating data to the new embeddable_hosts table. This is a one-way migration with no down method, meaning a rollback would leave the old application version without its configuration data. While this is intentional design (retiring obsolete settings), it's a legitimate architectural concern about rollback safety that a reviewer might flag. The migration does migrate data forward but provides no way to restore the old format if needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — [P1/100] "[0]['id'].to_i" Running the migration on a database without an embed_category setting matching an existing category returns zero rows and raises when indexing row zero, aborting the upgrade before the uncategorized fallback or host migration executes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 10-12 show: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If no embed_category setting exists or it doesn't match any category name, the query returns zero rows. Calling `[0]` on an empty result set will return nil, and then calling `['id']` on nil will raise an error (NoMethodError or similar), causing the migration to fail before reaching the fallback logic on lines 14-16 that handles category_id == 0. This is a real bug that would break migrations for users without the embed_category setting configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2/100] "host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));" Changing the still-enabled category chooser from A to B while a save of A is in flight makes the success callback display B as saved even though the server persisted A; rebuttal: the save and cancel buttons are disabled during the request; survives because: the category chooser remains enabled and the callback reads its current value instead of the saved request or response.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the category chooser remains enabled during save, but looking at the template (embeddable-host.hbs line 10), the cancel button is disabled with 'disabled=host.isSaving'. However, the category-chooser itself is NOT disabled during save - only the buttons are. But the finding's core claim is wrong: the callback uses 'this.get('categoryId')' which reads the component's categoryId property that was set in props before the save (line 33: 'props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')'). The save() call captures the categoryId at the time of the request. The success callback then uses the same categoryId value. While there's a theoretical race condition if the user could change the category during save, the finding incorrectly states the rebuttal is wrong - the save button IS disabled (line 9: 'disabled=cantSave' where cantSave includes isSaving). The category chooser not being disabled is a valid concern, but the finding's reasoning about the callback reading 'current value instead of saved request' is incorrect - it reads the same categoryId that was sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — [P2/100] "this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => {" A rejected DELETE request leaves an unhandled promise rejection with no deletion error rendered by this component, so the administrator receives no actionable explanation for the host remaining in the table; rebuttal: removal occurs only after success and a global rejection hook can log the error; survives because: neither logging nor retaining the row tells the administrator that deletion failed, and this action omits the popupAjaxError handler already used by save.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the delete action (lines 42-48 of embeddable-host.js.es6), the destroyRecord() promise has no .catch() handler, unlike the save() action which uses .catch(popupAjaxError). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user receives no feedback about the failure. This is a real defect - inconsistent error handling where save shows errors but delete silently fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15 — [P2/100] "host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first" Updating or deleting a host removed by another administrator dereferences nil in save_host or host.destroy and returns an unhandled server error instead of a missing-record response; rebuttal: the UI normally submits IDs from its loaded host list; survives because: that list remains stale after another session deletes a host and neither mutation action checks the lookup result.
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the update and destroy methods don't validate that EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns a valid record, and if it returns nil (e.g., when the host was deleted by another admin), calling methods like save_host or destroy on nil will cause an error (NoMethodError/unhandled server error). Both comments point to the same bug - missing nil check on the host lookup before using it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P2/75] "execute \"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\"" A legacy host value containing an apostrophe and SQL, such as https://example.com/',1,now(),now());DELETE/**/FROM/**/users;--, executes injected statements with the migration database role during upgrade; rebuttal: the legacy setting is administrator-controlled and typed host_list; survives because the prior allowlist explicitly accepts full URLs, this payload parses as an example.com URL, and this new raw SQL sink neither quotes stored values nor invokes the new model validation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SQL injection vulnerability in the migration file. Looking at line 25 of db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the code uses string interpolation to insert the host value directly into a SQL statement: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The variable `h` comes from splitting the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting value by newlines. While the old setting was typed as `host_list`, the code in app/models/site_setting.rb shows it accepted URLs with http:// prefixes. If an admin had stored a malicious value containing SQL injection payload (like an apostrophe followed by SQL commands), this migration would execute that injected SQL. The new EmbeddableHost model has validation, but the migration bypasses the model entirely using raw SQL execute. This is a legitimate security concern, though the attack surface is limited to admin-controlled data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P1/100] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" An unauthenticated embed request naming an allowed HTTP URL that redirects to http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ passes this replacement allowlist and makes TopicEmbed.find_remote fetch the internal endpoint through open(url).read, then publishes its extracted response as an imported topic; rebuttal: administrators choose the initial host and the old helper also lacked redirect checks; survives because an open redirect on that approved host supplies the internal destination, the modified retrieval gate remains responsible for approving untrusted embed URLs, and no redirect or resolved-address validation exists in the supplied fetch path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes an SSRF vulnerability where an allowed host with an open redirect could be exploited to fetch internal endpoints. However, examining the diff: 1) The `host_allowed?` method only checks if a host is in the allowlist - it doesn't fetch any URLs. 2) The `record_for_host` method extracts the host from a URI and checks against the database - no HTTP requests are made. 3) The actual URL fetching in `TopicEmbed` (not shown in full in this diff) would need to be examined separately. 4) The finding claims 'open(url).read' is used but this is not visible in the diff. 5) The old code (`SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`) had the same pattern of just checking hosts. The finding conflates the host validation logic with URL fetching logic that isn't shown in this diff, making claims about redirect handling that cannot be verified from the provided code.
